title: Introduce RAG micro-orchestrator sample for embedded SDKs and serverless tool call flow
author: Elena Park
description:
Motivation: teams building lightweight RAG experiences embedded in client apps (mobile/web) often need a minimal orchestrator that can run locally, spin up serverless tool call handlers, and produce deterministic traces for evals. This PR adds a compact 'micro-orchestrator' example that demonstrates: 1) an embedded TypeScript SDK shim that runs a decision loop in the browser while offloading heavy-tool calls to serverless endpoints, 2) a serverless handler pattern (AWS Lambda + express-like shim) for tool calling with idempotent retries and observability hooks, and 3) a deterministic test harness and replayable trace format compatible with the RAG scenario runner.

Summary of changes: added example project under examples/micro-orchestrator with a minimal UI, client SDK, serverless handlers, telemetry probe adaptors, and a small test harness. The sample focuses on readable code, a clear separation between the 'planner' (client decision loop) and the 'executor' (server tool-call service), and an e2e smoke scenario used by CI to validate streaming stability and structured output assertions. Also adds docs (walkthrough + architecture diagram) and a short migration note for teams using existing tool-calling patterns.

Checklist: - [x] Add micro-orchestrator example and README walkthrough - [x] Implement client shim with streaming + fallback policy - [x] Serverless tool-call handler with retry + idempotency token - [x] Telemetry probe hooks that emit compact traces compatible with rag-replay format - [x] e2e smoke tests in CI (headless browser) - [x] Docs site update linking to the new quickstart

Testing: unit tests for SDK logic, integration smoke test that runs the example in headless Chromium and validates three tool calls and a deterministic final answer, and replay verification against the included sample trace. CI runs on push and in PR: lint, build, unit, e2e-smoke. Local dev instructions included in README.

Compatibility notes: this example is intentionally minimal and uses the public Redwood SDK surface (redwood-js@>=1.6). The serverless handler uses a thin Express-like shim so it can be adapted to other runtimes. No breaking API changes are included.
commits: Add client SDK shim, streaming adapter and fallback policy
Implement serverless tool handler with idempotency and retry
Add replayable trace exporter and test harness
Docs: walkthrough, architecture diagram and quickstart link
Fix lint issues and tighten TypeScript types
Address review comments: telemetry hook names and test timeout tuning
review_comments: Aisha: Can we reduce the default e2e timeout? Long CI jobs block rollout. (author) Elena: lowered timeout from 90s to 45s and added retries for flaky network calls.
Miguel: The idempotency token generation should include a source hint to help debugging. (author) Elena: included source hint and added tests for token stability.
Claire: Docs look good but the architecture diagram needs clearer labelling for the telemetry path. (author) Elena: updated diagram and added a short section explaining the replayable trace format.
release_notes: Added a new micro-orchestrator example demonstrating an embedded RAG decision loop with serverless tool-call handlers, replayable traces for deterministic e2e tests, and telemetry probes. Useful as a starting point for teams embedding RAG behavior in client apps while offloading tool execution to server-side functions.
